Pitch 9, one of five central strips at Lord's, was handed its first demerit point and deemed "unsatisfactory" by the ICC after match referee Andy Pycroft found excessive seam movement and inconsistent bounce during this summer's Test against the Kiwis. All 40 wickets fell in just 166 overs during the match. The Jags were coming off a 1-15 season and an astonishing 11 losing campaigns out of the previous 13. They are one of just four teams in the NFL to have never played in a Super Bowl. Conversely, Lawrence arrived having won 34 of his 36 games in college and 52 of 54 in high school. He was supposed to bring those wins to Florida. metadata.summary: Spain have entered a bid for the 2035 Rugby World Cup, with Barcelona's Nou Camp or Real Madrid's Bernabeu in with a chance of hosting the final.
metadata.content: Rugby World Cup: Spain enter bid to host tournament - could Nou Camp or Bernabeu host 2035 final? | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby World Cup: Spain enter bid to host tournament - could Nou Camp or Bernabeu host 2035 final? Barcelona's Nou Camp or Real Madrid's Bernabeu could host the 2035 Rugby World Cup after Spain have entered a bid for the tournament along with Argentina and Japan; World Rugby are expected to announce a preferred bidder next year Thursday 15 October 2026 15:49, UK Image: The Nou Camp in Barcelona - which is currently undergoing renovations - could host the Rugby World Cup Final in 2035 Spain have entered a bid for the 2035 Rugby World Cup, with Barcelona's Nou Camp or Real Madrid's Bernabeu in with a chance of hosting the final. The home grounds of Barcelona and Real Madrid feature in the bid which would seek to use the venues and infrastructure from the 2030 FIFA World Cup, which Spain will co-host with Morocco and Portugal. In a statement, the Spanish Rugby Federation (RFER) said it aims to deliver the "best World Cup in history", with Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium and the Mestalla in Valencia also listed as possible other venues. messages.text: Haas sign Brazilian Camara as Ocon replacement

metadata.summary: Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will join Haas on a multi-year deal from the 2027 season as the Brazilian driver steps up to Formula 1.
metadata.content: Rafael Camara: Haas sign Brazilian Ferrari Academy driver to team for 2027 Formula 1 season on multi-year deal | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rafael Camara: Haas sign Brazilian Ferrari Academy driver to team for 2027 Formula 1 season on multi-year deal Rafael Camara has signed multi-year deal with Haas; the 21-year-old Brazilian is expected to drive alongside Britain's Oliver Bearman next season; Camara is replacing Esteban Ocon; watch every session of the United States GP on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 15 October 2026 15:35, UK Image: Rafael Camara will make his F1 debut with Haas next season Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will join Haas on a multi-year deal from the 2027 season as the Brazilian driver steps up to Formula 1. Camara, 21, has established himself as a rising star over recent years in the junior categories. He won last year's Formula 3 championship and leads this year's Formula 2 standings with two rounds of the season to go. He is a member of Ferrari's driver academy after joining in 2021, signing at the same time as fellow 21-year-old Oliver Bearman, who joined Haas in 2025 and remains on the Scuderia's books. Haas have not yet confirmed that Bearman will drive for them again in 2027 but team principal Ayao Komatsu says they expect to do so "very soon".
